newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt says U.S. relations good.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt says U.S. relations good.

text.p: The Australian government said on Monday Australia's relations with the United States were "in good shape" despite Australian Treasurer Peter Costello's controversial comments there last week.
"Mr Costello said the statements he made were on the basis of public information," Government Senate Leader Robert Hill told parliament.

"There was no leaking of anything said to him by American officials, therefore, there is no need for him to apologise or for us to apologise on his behalf and Australian-American relations are in good shape."
Last week, Costello revealed what were taken to be details of a private conversation with U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, moving world financial markets.
The incident caused the Australian opposition Labor Party to call for his resignation and won him few friends among his U.S. hosts.

Asked whether Costello's "arrogant" actions had breached the ministerial code of conduct, Hill said: "Mr Costello is not an arrogant man. He's quite a modest character actually and a very good treasurer."
Costello's revelation that the U.S. interest rate scene was unlikely to change caused a rally in the global bond market and also filtered through to key share markets.
Costello has denied that he revealed any confidential information, saying he only repeated what was already on the public record.
